summary.oneLiner: PSP Projects delivered record Q4 revenue (INR 1,115 Cr, +66% YoY) and a massive order book (INR 13,447 Cr, +85% YoY) driven by Adani Group mandates, though FY26 margins compressed to 6% due to project mix and a INR 29 Cr one-off ECL provision. The core investment thesis pivots to FY27 margin expansion (7-8% EBITDA) and PAT recovery as mobilization advances eliminate interest costs, targeting a debt-free status within 2-3 quarters.
summary.business: PSP Projects offers end-to-end construction and allied services in India, spanning design, civil works, MEP (mechanical, electrical and plumbing), facade development, interior fit-outs and operations & maintenance. It executes turnkey projects for industrial (pharmaceuticals, food processing, engineering, large-scale manufacturing), institutional (hospitals, education, retail, hospitality, corporate offices), government, government residential and private residential clients across India.

currentContext.strengths: Execution discipline and timely delivery positioned by management as the Company's core competitive advantage|In-house fleet of machinery and advanced precast/construction technologies strengthening delivery capability|Pan-India presence with order book diversified beyond its home state (31% from markets other than Gujarat as of March 31, 2026)|Long operating track record: 256 projects delivered and 94 under execution for 215+ customers as of March 31, 2026|Strategic equity partnership with Adani Infra (India) Limited, expected by management to be transformative for profitability and long-term sustainability|Credit rating of A+/Stable (long-term) and A1 (short-term) from CARE Ratings, reflecting financial discipline
currentContext.strategies: Evolving from a contractor executing drawings to a 'competitiveness partner' that engages at the design stage on commissioning urgency, capital efficiency, lifecycle implications and alternative engineering routes|Leveraging the equity partnership and joint control with the Adani Group to participate in a large, multi-year infrastructure investment cycle and undertake larger, more integrated EPC and general-contracting (GC) mode projects|Focus going forward on larger and more complex assignments, both within and outside the Adani Group, with an emphasis on maintaining margin discipline and strengthening cash flow generation|Increasing adoption of precast technologies to enhance execution efficiency and mitigate challenges related to labour mobilisation|Continuing diversification of the client mix across government and private-sector projects as a strategic priority, alongside a substantial and growing share from the Adani Group ecosystem|Strengthening counterparty risk review, concentration risk assessment, contract structuring safeguards, scenario planning, financial prudence in equipment acquisition and independent review mechanisms as the Company scales|Financial discipline prioritised, with internal accruals expected to fund a significant proportion of capital expenditure requirements|Refining medium-term planning across revenue aspirations, working-capital-cycle optimisation, return on capital employed trajectory and a disciplined capital allocation framework
currentContext.expansion: PSP is expanding its precast concrete manufacturing footprint (PSP Precast, located within a proposed 62-acre industrial campus on Sanand-Nalsarovar Road, Gujarat) by an additional 100,000 square feet (1 Lakh sq ft), adding hollow-core beds and advanced mould systems to increase annual production capacity and product diversity for high-rise and industrial segments. Plans are also underway to supply cut-to-size reinforcement steel directly from the precast facility to project sites across Ahmedabad and Gandhinagar, Gujarat. Over a five-year strategic outlook, the Company aims to increase precast revenue contribution, expand capacity in line with order visibility, reduce carbon intensity, enhance digital production automation, and deepen integration with the construction, industrial and infrastructure segments; management states this expansion is guided by capex-allocation discipline (utilisation thresholds, order visibility and return benchmarks) rather than speculative growth.
currentContext.mdna: Opportunity anchored in the Adani Group's announced investment blueprint, with cumulative capital deployment expected to exceed INR 600,000 Crore over the next 5-7 years, creating a large multi-year infrastructure opportunity set|Order conversion momentum expected to strengthen further, supported by improved market access and execution capabilities following the Adani Group association|Company expects a gradual increase in participation in projects within the broader Adani Group ecosystem (airports, roads, industrial assets, healthcare infrastructure, ports, data centres, residential developments), while continuing to pursue opportunities across external clients|Increasing adoption of pass-through clauses in the order book mitigates commodity-price volatility exposure; commodity price volatility during the year was managed through applicable price-variation mechanisms, with minimal margin impact on Adani Group-related projects and limited index-linked adjustments on government fixed-price contracts|EBITDA margin moderation during the year (7.21% to 6.00%) attributed to the impact of provisioning towards expected credit losses on contract assets, alongside an evolving project mix amid execution scale-up|A sequential improvement in performance during the latter part of the year is cited by management as an early indication of stabilisation in operating metrics|Company positioned to deliver a step-up in revenue going forward, with improving operational traction as projects progress, based on the strength of the existing order book and execution pipeline|Closing order book of INR 13,447 Crore as of March 31, 2026, up from an opening INR 7,266 Crore, after securing fresh orders of INR 10,925 Crore during FY26 (an increase of approximately 85% over the opening balance) — the highest order inflow in any financial year|Approximately 67% of the order book pertains to the Adani Group, with the balance 33% from external clients|Order book diversified with about 25% from government projects and 75% from private-sector clients (per CFO commentary); category-wise breakup per the Board's Report shows Institutional 38.22%, Residential 35.48%, Government 24.61% and Industrial 1.70%|Geographically, Gujarat accounts for about 69% of the order book, Maharashtra approximately 24-25%, with smaller shares from Karnataka, Delhi, Uttar Pradesh and other states|94 projects under execution as of March 31, 2026, spread mainly across Gujarat, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh and Delhi|Major new orders secured during FY26 include development works at SVPI Airport, Ahmedabad (INR 2,299 Crore), Matunga Rehab Building, Mumbai (INR 2,026 Crore), Mahim Renewal Building at Dharavi, Mumbai (INR 1,303 Crore), and development of Shree Ambaji Mata Temple, Dist. Banaskantha (INR ~966-967 Crore)|Order book provides multi-year execution visibility, supporting capacity planning and equipment deployment optimisation

risks.note: During FY26, sales to a single customer/group of customers approximated 33.26% of revenue from operations (up from 12.34% in FY25), and receivables from that customer were 34.66% of total receivables (up from 17.92% in FY25); the Group states a loss of this customer could significantly affect operating results or cash flow. Management separately flags market and client concentration risk, citing cyclical demand and reliance on large clients as a factor that may affect order inflows, mitigated by a diversified order book and strong client relationships.

EPC/construction projects require significant working capital (mobilisation advances, milestone billing, retention money); mitigation relies on disciplined billing, receivables management and prudent leverage to support liquidity stability.

Complex projects involve coordination challenges, evolving designs and site constraints that may impact timelines and margins; mitigated through structured planning, milestone monitoring, engineering capability and technical audits.
Increasing contract sizes may lead to margin variability and execution complexity; mitigated by selective bidding, exposure limits and senior leadership oversight in project selection.

risks.risk: Input cost and supply chain risk
risks.note: Volatility in key construction materials may affect project costs; mitigated by long-term vendor relationships, diversified sourcing and value engineering.

risks.risk: Government and urban infrastructure segment risk
risks.note: This segment is assessed as moderate-to-high risk (higher than other segments) due to regulatory approvals, land handover timing and milestone-based payment structures.

Greater reliance on digital systems and project dashboards increases cyber exposure; mitigated by secure IT systems, real-time monitoring and employee awareness, though scale of investment/incident history is not separately disclosed beyond a statement that no breaches occurred in FY26.

Cost overruns or delayed collections may affect profitability; the Group's expected credit loss allowance on trade receivables rose to INR 3,609.73 Lakhs as at March 31, 2026 from INR 2,161.92 Lakhs a year earlier, alongside a rise in receivables aged more than 360 days, reflecting collection risk embedded in the EPC billing cycle.

one-line thesis: PSP Projects delivered record Q4 revenue (INR 1,115 Cr, +66% YoY) and a massive order book (INR 13,447 Cr, +85% YoY) driven by Adani Group mandates, though FY26 margins compressed to 6% due to project mix and a INR 29 Cr one-off ECL provision. The core investment thesis pivots to FY27 margin expansion (7-8% EBITDA) and PAT recovery as mobilization advances eliminate interest costs, targeting a debt-free status within 2-3 quarters.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 1,115 Cr (Q4, +66% YoY), INR 3,149 Cr (FY26, +25% YoY). EBITDA: INR 60 Cr (Q4, +85% YoY, 5.4% margin); INR 189 Cr (FY26, +5% YoY, 6.0% margin vs 7.1% prior). PAT: INR 21 Cr (Q4, +244% YoY); INR 55 Cr (FY26, -2% YoY). Order Book: INR 13,447 Cr (+85% YoY). Net Debt: ~INR 143 Cr (Gross Debt INR 317 Cr less Cash/FD INR 176 Cr free + lien deposits); Distortion: FY26 PAT impacted by INR 29 Cr ECL provision on Kashi project (unbilled >1 year) and high interest costs (INR 45 Cr) expected to vanish in FY27.
guidance: Revenue: INR 4,500 Cr for FY27. EBITDA Margin: 7-8% band. Order Inflow: INR 5,000-6,000 Cr from Adani Group + INR 1,000-2,000 Cr external potential. Capex: INR 120-150 Cr (approx. 3% of revenue).
order book & pipeline: INR 13,447 Cr total; 67% (INR 9,000 Cr) from Adani Group, 33% (INR 4,300 Cr) external. Key projects: Shree Ambaji Mata Temple (INR 966 Cr), SMC Highrise (INR 731 Cr), GIFT City Fintech Building (INR 261 Cr), Human & Biological Science Gallery (INR 254 Cr), Sabarmati River Front Phase II (INR 218 Cr), Dharoi Dam Region (INR 223 Cr). Bid pipeline: INR 6,600 Cr (60% group, 40% external).
segment / subsidiary detail: Institutional (Gati Shakti Univ, Science City), Industrial (Airport dev, Fintech building), Residential (GIFT City high-rise, Matunga rehab), Government (Sabarmati Riverfront, Dharoi Dam). Precast facility utilization high; executed 122m residential tower and Project 90 (18 floors in 148 days).
growth verticals / optionality: Upside from Commonwealth Games stadium tender (INR 7,000-8,000 Cr potential, expected soon); expansion of precast capacity with minimal capex (INR 15-20 Cr for equipment) if order flow exceeds 3M sqft/year; penetration into non-Gujarat markets via large institutional bids.
margins & cost dynamics: FY26 margin compression (6% vs 7.1% prior) due to low-margin ramp-up phase of large projects and INR 29 Cr ECL provision. FY27 guidance 7-8% supported by pass-through material contracts with Adani (mitigating inflation/war risk) and operating leverage. Employee cost expected to grow in line with revenue (2-4% of sales) as hiring stabilizes.
capex / expansion: FY26 Capex: INR 192 Cr. FY27 Guidance: INR 120-150 Cr. Primarily for machinery/equipment to support precast and project execution; shed infrastructure already in place. Depreciation expected to rise slightly with new assets but stabilizes as % of sales.
capital allocation: Priority on becoming debt-free within 2-3 quarters by utilizing INR 814 Cr interest-free mobilization advances from Adani to repay INR 317 Cr gross debt. Surplus cash to be deployed in working capital and potential minor precast equipment upgrades. No dividend policy change discussed.
risks & watch-items: High concentration risk (67% order book from Adani Group); Execution delays in Mumbai projects (Matunga, Mahim) due to regulatory approvals/tree cutting; Potential further ECL provisions on UP Medical College projects (INR 60 Cr unbilled + INR 40 Cr receivable) if settlements drag; Working capital strain if non-Adani receivables (currently ~90-100 days) do not normalize to 60 days.
management quality / tone: Confident on execution scale and order visibility; Conservative on margin guidance (7-8%) to account for variability; Optimistic on balance sheet repair (debt-free target) and cash flow improvement due to favorable group payment terms; Transparent regarding one-off provisions (Kashi) and legacy receivable challenges (UP, SDB).
non-obvious takeaways: The INR 814 Cr mobilization advance is entirely interest-free, acting as a massive working capital subsidy that will structurally lower finance costs to near-zero, effectively converting previous interest expenses (INR 45 Cr) directly into PAT. The 'margin compression' is largely an accounting artifact of front-loading provisions and ramp-up costs, masking the underlying cash profitability of the new order mix.

themes.title: Infrastructure EPC & roads order-book conversion
themes.need: India's record capital-outlay cycle (roads, metro, marine, hydro, tunnelling) gives diversified EPC contractors multi-year visibility - AFCONS tracks a ~INR4 lakh cr pipeline (70% domestic) and targets ~INR30,000cr FY27 inflow; NCC/DBL/PNCINFRA/GRINFRA/ASHOKA/CEIGALL carry large road/HAM books; AFCONS/PATELENG/AHLUCONT/PSPPROJECT add marine, hydro and building EPC. The binding issue is execution + client-payment cycles, not order intake.
themes.driver: L1-to-firm-order conversion (AFCONS Croatia/Vadhavan, DMRC awards); NHAI/HAM award pickup; monsoon-end execution ramp.
